children: stock fell as much as 8.7% on Wednesday, its biggest intraday percentage drop in over a year, following Chairman Om Prakash Bhatt's resignation  after an internal audit into a board evaluation found concerns.
The stock fell to as low as 1,780.70 rupees, with the sharp decline putting it among the top losers on the Nifty IT index
Bhatt, who previously served as chairman of India's largest lender, State Bank of India, was appointed chair of Coforge's board in 2024 with a term due to finish in April 2027.

An audit into the board evaluation process and the resulting report, which were handled under Bhatt's guidance, identified concerns about how the report "had been dealt with and presented to the board", the company said. This included concerns that material information about Bhatt's own performance had not been fully disclosed to the board.
The company did not elaborate on the specific nature of the information about Bhatt's performance that had not been disclosed to the board.
The board raised its concerns with Bhatt and was evaluating his response when Bhatt tendered his resignation on September 8.
In his resignation letter, which was included in the regulatory filing, Bhatt maintained that he had acted in good faith.

"I believe that continuing on the Board while there remains a disagreement considering the characteristics of my good faith actions in the Board evaluation process would not be conducive to the effective functioning of the Board," Bhatt said in the letter.
Coforge named Vivek Sharma, a non-executive independent director, as interim chair until January 31, 2027.
Coforge's shares were down 6.22% at 1,828.80 rupees apiece as of 9:37 a.m. IST.
